# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to relay what I see to Blind (who can hear me) and Mute (who can hear me too, but can't act). Let me share the bomb's details clearly since this is the first turn and nobody knows anything yet.

Since Blind can hear me but Mute holds the manual and needs to guide us, I should speak this info so both Mute and Blind get it (Mute can't speak back, only gesture to me, so I need to give Blind the full picture now while also signaling Mute).

```
speak(text="I see the bomb now. Display shows the number 3. Light is green. There are 3 wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

Mute is gesturing to me — three ☝-like taps (👆👆👆). Since Mute can't speak to me but can gesture, and gestures carry limited info, this likely means "wire 3" (pointing three times, or pointing to position 3) or "display shows 3, confirmed" or could be asking me to point at wire number 3 specifically.

Given Mute holds the manual and knows what matters, three repeated 👆 gestures most plausibly indicates "wire #3" — drawing attention to the third wire specifically. This may be Mute's way of asking me to confirm or focus on wire 3, or telling Blind (via me relaying) that wire 3 is the one to cut.

Since I can't be sure of exact meaning yet, I should acknowledge and relay to Blind what I know, while also trying to prompt Mute for more (though Mute can't speak). I'll describe wire 3's color again to reinforce, and let Blind know Mute seems to be pointing at wire 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just gestured toward something three times, possibly pointing at wire 3, which is green. Wait for more before acting.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

Same gesture repeated: 👆👆👆 from Mute to me again. This is likely a stable signal, not a one-off — perhaps Mute is trying to establish a code with me since we can't understand each other's channel content directly (I don't hear speech, Mute can't speak or see gestures back from me... wait, Mute CAN see gestures if I make them, since Mute is not deaf/blind - Mute just can't speak or touch).

Let me reconsider: Mute can read the manual, cannot speak, cannot touch bomb. Mute presumably CAN see and hear normally otherwise. So Mute can see my gestures and hear my speech. Mute is gesturing to me since that's Mute's only output to me (can't speak).

Three 👆 repeated consistently suggests this is a deliberate fixed signal - maybe encoding "3" (matching the display of 3), confirming they see/know the display is 3, or indicating "wire 3" is significant per the manual.

I should gesture back to Mute to establish two-way gesture communication, confirming what I see, since Mute can see my gestures too.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👆", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute keeps repeating a three-part gesture, likely confirming display is 3 or pointing at wire 3, which is green. Still waiting for clearer signal before you act.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👍]

Now Mute added a 👍 after the three 👆's: [👆 👆 👆 👍]. This looks like confirmation — "three, yes/correct" — likely confirming that "3" (matching display, or wire 3) is the right answer per the manual. My gesture of ✌👆👍 (meaning "2? no, 3, good") seems to have gotten a "yes" back specifically to the "three" idea.

So it seems: display=3 matches manual instructions, and the 👍 confirms this interpretation. This strongly suggests the manual says something keyed to "3" — possibly "cut wire 3" or "the number 3 is safe/correct".

I should tell Blind: wire 3 (green) is very likely the one to cut, since Mute is confirming "3" is correct.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirmed with a thumbs up after repeating three taps. Strong signal that the number 3 matters and matches the display. I believe wire 3, which is green, is the one to cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

Mute repeated the plain three-tap gesture again [👆 👆 👆] without the thumbs up this time. This might mean my previous message to Blind hasn't been acted on yet, or Mute is re-confirming since Blind hasn't responded/acted. Since Blind's actions aren't shown to me (I only see gestures from Mute), I don't know if Blind has cut anything yet.

I'll keep reinforcing to Blind that wire 3 is likely correct, and gesture back to Mute to confirm I still understand "three" is the key number.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is still signaling three, consistent with wire 3, the green wire, matching the display of 3. If you haven't acted yet, cutting wire 3 seems like our best bet based on this repeated confirmation.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👉]

Now Mute shows [👆 👆 👆 👉] — three taps followed by a "point right" gesture. This could mean "three, then/next" or could be indicating a sequence, or perhaps "wire 3, point/proceed" — encouraging action to proceed with wire 3.

The 👉 might signal "go ahead" or "next step" or could be pointing to something specific like "to the right" (position-wise, if wires are numbered left to right, wire 3 might be rightmost).

This reinforces the "3" signal with an added "proceed/point" gesture, suggesting confirmation to move forward with cutting wire 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute added a pointing gesture after the three taps this time, which I read as a signal to proceed. I still believe wire 3, the green wire, is correct. If you have not cut it yet, go ahead and cut wire 3.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👉"])
wait()
```
